description.value: The study estimated resting-state effective connectivity among default mode, salience, and central executive network regions across cognitively normal, early mild cognitive impairment, late mild cognitive impairment, and Alzheimer's disease groups, and tested whether connectivity predicted cognitive scores.

spans.text: We used PEB to infer the connectivity strengths for the four subject groups.
A linear regression analysis was also carried out to test if EC between regions could predict subjects' cognitive scores.

design.value: A cross-sectional comparison of four stable participant groups using longitudinally documented resting-state fMRI records from the ADNI-2 phase, with group-level PEB/DCM estimation, ANOVA comparisons, and linear regression of connectivity against cognitive scores.

spans.text: We selected four types of subjects, whose general inclusion/exclusion criteria are as follows: (1) CN subjects: MMSE scores above 24, CDR = 0, free of memory complaints; (2) EMCI patients: MMSE scores above 24, CDR = 0.5, have subjective memory complaints, abnormal memory functions; (3) LMCI patients: MMSE scores above 24, CDR = 0.5, have subjective memory complaints, abnormal memory functions (more severe compared to EMCIs); (4) AD patients: MMSE scores ranging from 20 to 26, CDR above 0.5, have subjective memory complaints, abnormal memory functions (same as LMCIs).
All subjects remained in their progression stage (stable) throughout the entire data collection visits (spanning for at least 24 months).
Data used in this study were obtained from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) database ( adni.loni.usc.edu ).

model_type.value: dynamic causal modeling (DCM) with parametric empirical Bayes (PEB)

spans.text: We used PEB to infer the connectivity strengths for the four subject groups.
Bayesian Model Reduction (BMR) was used to control the switching on and off of each connection
The generalized BOLD signal model was proposed by Stephan et al. ( 2007 )

model_settings.value: Seven ROI nodes: mPFC and bilateral PCC, dlPFC, and ACC; ROI activity was summarized from all voxels within an 8-mm-radius sphere around associated MNI coordinates.

spans.text: To include regions from DMN, SAN, and CEN networks, mPFC and bilateral PCC, dlPFC, ACC were chosen as regions of interest
We summarized ROI activity by extracting time series at all voxels within a sphere having radius 8 mm around an associated MNI coordinate for the ROI.
3.2. Connectivity at group level

Bayesian Model Reduction (BMR) was used to control the switching on and off of each connection (to calculate the likelihood with the connection's presence and absence) and estimate the parameter to infer the connectivity pattern.
The preprocessing was carried out using Statistical Parametric Mapping 12 (SPM 12, http://www.fil.ion.ucl.ac.uk/spm ) and RESTplus toolkits (Jia et al., 2019 ).
The connectivity strengths for each subject group were compared using analysis of variance (ANOVA).

model_settings.value: Bonferroni correction was applied for multiple comparisons.

spans.text: Bonferroni correction was applied for multiple comparisons.
ANOVA of the effective connection strengths showed only connections L-PCC → L-PCC, R-PCC → R-ACC, and R-ACC → R-ACC were significantly different within subject groups.
A linear regression analysis was also carried out to test if EC between regions could predict subjects' cognitive scores.
